Q5(a) : « share of profit to debenture holders / preference share holders » lu comme l'intérêt fixe de 5 % sur 1 200 000 FCFA (60 000 FCFA) et le dividende fixe de 6 % sur 1 000 000 FCFA (60 000 FCFA), recalculés avec Python ; le taux de dividende des actions ordinaires n'est pas donné, l'impôt sur les bénéfices est ignoré, et le solde de 680 000 FCFA n'est cité qu'à titre d'information.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the capital structure of AYZ Company Limited.

1,200,000 FCFA Debenture at 5%

1,000,000 FCFA Preference shares at 6%

10,000,000 FCFA Ordinary shares

AYZ in 2010, made a profit of 800,000 FCFA.

(a) Calculate the share of profit to;

(i) Debenture holders.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Debenture holders are lenders: they receive a **fixed interest** of 5% per year on the value of their debentures, whatever the profit.

$$
\text{Interest} = \dfrac{5}{100} \times 1,200,000 = 60,000 \text{ FCFA}
$$

**The debenture holders receive 60,000 FCFA** (the profit of 800,000 FCFA is more than enough to pay it).

Preference shareholders receive a **fixed dividend** of 6% on their shares, paid out of profit **after the debenture interest** and **before** the ordinary shareholders receive anything.

$$
\text{Preference dividend} = \dfrac{6}{100} \times 1,000,000 = 60,000 \text{ FCFA}
$$

**The preference shareholders receive 60,000 FCFA.**

(The balance of the profit, $800,000 - 60,000 - 60,000 = 680,000$ FCFA, remains for the ordinary shareholders, as dividend and retained profit.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) Determine the amount of total capital raised from the sales of the different securities.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total capital is the sum of the amounts raised by selling each type of security (debentures, preference shares and ordinary shares).

$$
\text{Total capital} = 1,200,000 + 1,000,000 + 10,000,000 = 12,200,000 \text{ FCFA}
$$

| Security | Amount raised (FCFA) |
|---|---|
| Debentures | 1,200,000 |
| Preference shares | 1,000,000 |
| Ordinary shares | 10,000,000 |
| **Total** | **12,200,000** |

**The total capital raised is 12,200,000 FCFA.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Make a distinction between Ordinary shareholders and debenture holders.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Ordinary shareholders** are the **owners** of the company, who buy shares in it. **Debenture holders** are **lenders** (creditors) to the company, who buy debentures (loan certificates). The differences are as follows.

| Basis | Ordinary shareholders | Debenture holders |
|---|---|---|
| Status | Owners of the company | Creditors who lend money to it |
| Return | Dividend, **variable**, depending on profit; none if there is no profit | Interest, **fixed**, paid whether or not the company makes a profit |
| Risk | High: they are the last to be paid and bear the losses | Low: they are paid before shareholders |
| Voting rights | Yes, they vote at the annual general meeting and elect the directors | No voting rights and no control of the company |
| Security | No security | Often secured on the assets of the company |
| On liquidation | Paid last, from what remains | Paid before the shareholders |
| Repayment | Capital is not repaid by the company during its life | Repaid on a fixed date (redeemable) |
| Gains | Share in the growth of the company: capital gains and high dividends in good years | No share in the growth: the return is limited to the interest |
| In the accounts | Dividend is a share-out of profit | Interest is an expense of the company, paid before tax |

(Four distinctions, each with both sides, are enough for full marks.)
